stem.text: In this question, alkenes and cyclic alkanes should be considered.
How many structural isomers of C4H8 are there?

explanation.text: C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub> has one degree of unsaturation, so each isomer has either one C=C bond or one ring. The straight-chain alkenes are but-1-ene and but-2-ene; the branched alkene is methylpropene. The rings are cyclobutane and methylcyclopropane.
Cis- and trans-but-2-ene are stereoisomers: they have the same structural formula and differ only in spatial arrangement. They therefore count once when counting structural isomers.

optionAnalysis.text: Three is the number of alkenes only (but-1-ene, but-2-ene, methylpropene); it leaves out the two cyclic alkanes the question says to include.
Four usually comes from missing methylcyclopropane, or from counting only some of the rings and chains.
But-1-ene, but-2-ene, methylpropene, cyclobutane and methylcyclopropane: five structural isomers.
Six counts cis- and trans-but-2-ene separately. They are geometrical isomers, not structural isomers.

reasoningChain: C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub> = C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n</sub>: either one C=C or one ring.
Do not split but-2-ene into cis and trans, because the question asks for structural isomers.

inferredMistakes.text: Forgetting methylcyclopropane and stopping at four isomers.
Counting cis- and trans-but-2-ene as two isomers and getting six.

bullets: Option B was a common incorrect answer.

The structural isomers of C4H8 that are alkenes or cyclic alkanes are:
• But-1-ene
• But-2-ene
• Methylpropene
• Cyclobutane
• Methylcyclopropane.

Since the question specifies structural isomers the two geometrical isomers of but-2-ene are considered as a single isomer. There are five structural isomers, so the correct option is C.
